TEXT.TEXTVALUE: We require zinc strip, copper strip, 1M ZnSO[sub]4[/sub] solution, voltmeter, 1M CuSO[sub]4[/sub] solution, salt bridge, connecting wires, sand paper, etc.
Clean it with the help of sand paper.
Dip the copper strip in to the beaker containing 1M copper sulphate solution.
Similarly, take the zinc strip and clean it with sand paper.
Then dip it into another beaker containing 1M zinc sulphate solution.
Connect the two solutions through the salt bridge. [Salt bridge is an inverted U-tube filled with a solution of inert electrolytes like K[sub]2[/sub]SO[sub]4[/sub], KCl, KNO[sub]3[/sub] etc.
Now,connect the positive terminal of the voltmeter with the copper strip using connecting wire.
Note the position of the pointer in the voltmeter.
Connect the negative terminal of the voltmeter with the zinc strip using another connecting wire.
Note the position of the pointer in the voltmeter and record the reading.
This value gives the E.M.F of the cell.
Repeat the experiment by taking different concentrations of zinc sulphate and copper sulphate solutions.

From the observations it is clear that E.M.F of the cell increases with decrease in concentration of the electrolyte around anode (zinc electrode) and increase in concentration of the electrolyte around cathode (copper electrode).
